group.passage: More than a quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level, and without its dunes and dikes, over half of the country would be under water. Much of this land was not given by nature but won from it. Especially in the seventeenth century, the Dutch turned whole lakes into dry land, and the work of keeping that land dry has never really stopped. In the northern part of Holland, sea water had once flowed into the land through open inlets. When these inlets were closed off, the water left behind formed lakes. Some of the lakes were far from peaceful neighbors. Storms kept eating away at their shores, and one lake near Haarlem grew from about 6,600 to 19,500 hectares between 1530 and 1730. People had a name for a lake that behaved in this way: a “water wolf.” Draining a lake took money, skill, and wind. First, workers built a dike all the way around it. Then they put up windmills, which pumped the water out of the lake. One such project was the Beemster, a lake in North Holland that was pumped dry in 1612, creating about 7,100 hectares of new land. Companies of investors paid for such work, and the rich clay soil they uncovered was sold to wealthy townspeople for farming. Between 1546 and 1650, more than seventy lakes in the region were drained in this way. The water wolf near Haarlem had to wait much longer: it was not drained until the age of steam. Work began in 1840, and by 1852 three steam pumping stations had emptied it, leaving a polder of 18,500 hectares. Winning the land, however, was only the beginning. Compared with the sea, the ground in the Low Countries slowly sinks, by about ten centimeters every century, so water has to be pumped out again and again. Today, water boards that date back to the Middle Ages still run the pumps that keep these polders dry.

translation_zh.text:
荷蘭人的圩田

荷蘭有超過四分之一的土地低於海平面；要是沒有沙丘和堤防，全國一半以上的土地都會泡在水裡。這些土地有很多不是大自然給的，而是從大自然手中贏來的。尤其在十七世紀，荷蘭人把整座湖泊變成陸地，而讓這些土地保持乾燥的工作，從來沒有真正停過。

在荷蘭省（Holland）北部，海水曾經從敞開的海灣流進陸地。這些海灣被封閉之後，留下來的水就形成了湖泊。有些湖可一點也不是安分的鄰居。暴風不斷侵蝕湖岸，哈勒姆（Haarlem）附近的一座湖在 1530 年到 1730 年間，從大約 6,600 公頃擴大到 19,500 公頃。人們替用這種方式行事的湖取了個名字：「水狼」。

抽乾一座湖需要金錢、技術和風。首先，工人沿著湖的四周築起一圈堤防。接著豎起風車，把湖裡的水抽出去。貝姆斯特（Beemster）就是這樣的一項工程：這座位於北荷蘭的湖在 1612 年被抽乾，造出大約 7,100 公頃的新土地。這類工程由投資者組成的公司出錢，抽乾後露出的肥沃黏土則賣給富有的城裡人耕種。1546 年到 1650 年間，這一帶有七十多座湖用這種方式被抽乾。

哈勒姆附近的那頭「水狼」則等了更久：它直到蒸汽時代才被抽乾。工程在 1840 年開始，到了 1852 年，三座蒸汽抽水站把湖水抽乾，留下一片 18,500 公頃的圩田。

然而，贏得土地只是開始。和海平面相比，低地國的地面正緩慢下沉，每一百年大約下沉十公分，所以水必須一再被抽出去。今天，起源於中世紀的水利會仍然操作著抽水機，讓這些圩田保持乾燥。
